name: couril

attributes.attribute: caught travelers and made them dance to death
left a young woman with a half-fairy child

sources: Henderson, George. Survivals in Belief Among the Celts. Glasgow: James MacLeose and Sons, 1911, 73.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The courils were Breton fairies. They were wicked, or plainly mischievous, and they gathered around the old stone circles, most of all those at Tresmalonen, where they danced all night. A traveler who neared them in the dark was taken and made to dance until he fell dead from exhaustion. If the lost traveler was a young woman, the fairies enjoyed her favor and left her with child, a half-fairy child.

okr.objective: The courils are mischievous Breton fairies of the stone circles.
key_results: The courils were Breton fairies, evil and full of tricks.
They gathered around stone circles and danced all night.
A traveler they caught danced until exhaustion killed him.
A captured young woman bore a half-fairy child.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
